channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekneftgaz and CNPC Discuss Fuel Supply and M-25 Field Accident
item.description: Uzbekneftgaz Chairman Abdug'ani Sanginov met with a CNPC delegation led by President Zhou Xinhuai on October 20. They reviewed joint results in drilling, exploration, seismic research, enhancing gas field efficiency, and equipment supply. A key topic was addressing the accident at the M-25 gas field in Surkhandarya region.

item.title: Egypt Eases Entry Requirements for Kazakhstan Tourists Following Ministerial Agreement
item.description: Egypt has agreed to simplify entry requirements for citizens of Kazakhstan, removing them from a list of Central Asian countries with additional conditions. The agreement was reached during a meeting between the foreign ministers of both nations. While visa regimes will be maintained, the specifics of the new procedures and their effective date remain unclear.

item.title: Russia Bans Entry for Over 260,000 Foreigners in First Eight Months of 2026, a 75.8% Increase
item.description: Russia has banned entry for over 260,000 foreigners and stateless persons from January to August 2026, a 75.8% increase compared to the same period in 2025. The bans are primarily due to administrative expulsion, overstaying previous visits, providing false information, or failing to pay taxes and fines. Security-related entry denials also quadrupled.

item.title: Over 1.3 Billion Tenge Recovered from Contractors After Aktobe State Procurement Audit
item.description: An audit of state procurement in Aktobe has uncovered violations causing damages to state interests, resulting in the recovery of over 1.3 billion tenge from contractors. The prosecutor's office found that clients failed to collect payments from non-compliant contractors for urban infrastructure projects. Over 556 million tenge was overpaid for special equipment but has since been fully returned to the budget.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's National Bank Fines Two Payment Organizations Over 6 Million Som
item.description: The National Bank of Kyrgyzstan has fined two payment organizations a total of 6.185 million soms for violating anti-money laundering and counter-terrorism financing laws. One firm was fined 5.38 million soms for inadequate client due diligence during international electronic money transfers, while the second received an 804,130 som penalty for similar violations.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Switzerland to Enhance Cooperation on Critical Raw Materials
item.description: Switzerland has proposed developing cooperation with Kazakhstan in critical raw materials and signing a memorandum of understanding. The initiative was discussed at the 12th meeting of the Kazakh-Swiss Intergovernmental Commission on Trade and Economic Cooperation in Bern. Kazakhstan expressed interest in increasing agricultural exports and invited Swiss companies to invest in various sectors.

item.title: Rare Animal Rehabilitation Center Opens in Kyrgyzstan's Issyk-Kul Region
item.description: A scientific research and rehabilitation center for rare animals, named 'Ak Ilbirs', has opened in the village of Ananyevo, Issyk-Kul region. The center will focus on conserving the snow leopard and other rare species, conducting research, providing veterinary care, and rehabilitating animals. The opening ceremony was attended by Kyrgyzstan's Cabinet Chairman and the Rais of Tatarstan.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Health Ministry Discusses Corruption Risks in Healthcare Services
item.description: The Kyrgyz Ministry of Health has identified corruption risks in healthcare, particularly concerning patient hospitalization, surgeries, and obtaining medical certificates or sick leave. Officials noted that patients might be told there are no beds or offered to pay unofficial fees to speed up services. The ministry encourages reporting corruption with evidence.

item.title: International Court Rejects Kazakhstan's $12 Billion Claim in Kashagan Dispute
item.description: An international arbitration court has rejected Kazakhstan's claim of approximately $12 billion against foreign shareholders of the North Caspian Operating Company (NCOC) related to disputed expenses at the Kashagan oil field. The court cited the claim was filed too late. However, another claim totaling around $8 billion will be considered.

item.title: Four Islamic and Three European Foreign Ministers to Meet in Istanbul on Middle East Issues
item.description: Foreign ministers from four Islamic countries and three European nations will convene in Istanbul to discuss the Strait of Hormuz and the Middle East crisis. Pakistan's foreign ministry confirmed participation from Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Egypt, the UK, Germany, and France. Discussions will cover regional and international developments.

item.title: US Proposes Unequal Peace Deal for Russia-Ukraine Conflict, Report Claims
item.description: The US is reportedly pressuring Kyiv to accept an "unequal peace agreement" to resolve the Russia-Ukraine conflict, according to The Economist. Proposals include a demilitarized zone in Donbas, economic cooperation between the US and Russia, and Ukraine's EU membership in exchange for not joining NATO. Europe has rejected a proposal to resume Russian gas supplies.

item.title: Kazakhstan President Tokayev awards over a thousand citizens for Republic Day
item.description: On the eve of Republic Day, Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev signed a decree awarding state honors to over a thousand citizens. The awards recognize contributions to the country's socio-economic and cultural development, strengthening public accord, and active public service. Recipients include veterans, workers, business representatives, educators, scientists, medical professionals, and military personnel.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Lawsuit Against Kashagan Oil Companies Rejected
item.description: A lawsuit filed by Kazakhstan against oil companies operating at the Kashagan field has been dismissed. The details of the lawsuit and the reasons for its rejection were not immediately available.

item.title: ADB provides $20.5 million loan to Tajikistan for pension system digitalization
item.description: The Government of Tajikistan and the Asian Development Bank (ADB) have signed an agreement for a $20.5 million loan. This funding will support the modernization and digitalization of the social insurance and pension system in Tajikistan.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Parliament Speaker Marlen Mamataliev visits Japan to boost cooperation
item.description: Marlen Mamataliev, Speaker of the Jogorku Kenesh, began an official visit to Japan, meeting with the Speaker of Japan's House of Representatives. Discussions focused on strengthening inter-parliamentary ties, economic relations, and cultural exchanges.

item.title: Kazakhstan Allocates Up to 50 University Study Places Annually for Kyrgyzstan Citizens
item.description: Kazakhstan offers up to 50 university study places annually for citizens of Kyrgyzstan. Of these, 30 are for Kyrgyz citizens and up to 20 for ethnic Kazakhs with Kyrgyz citizenship. Quotas are allocated for IT, engineering, construction, agriculture, medicine, and pedagogy, with specific numbers for bachelor's and master's programs.

item.title: Criminal group faces trial in Astana for defrauding 51 citizens
item.description: A criminal group of seven individuals in Astana is facing trial for large-scale fraud. Over four years, they allegedly defrauded 51 citizens by promising help with housing programs, loans, and financing. The total material damage exceeded 413 million tenge. The group is charged with fraud and creating/leading an organized crime group.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Sadyr Japarov discusses demanding work schedule
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov addressed a citizen's complaint about not being able to secure an appointment, stating, 'You are 7.5 million, I am one.' He described his demanding work schedule, working 20 hours a day after only 4 hours of sleep. Japarov emphasized his commitment to his duties despite the intense workload.

item.title: Tajikistan: Man sentenced to five and a half years for driving wife to suicide
item.description: A man in Tajikistan's Devashtich district has been sentenced to five and a half years in a high-security prison for driving his wife to suicide. The sentence was reduced by nearly two years due to an amnesty law. The court found the 22-year-old guilty of cruel treatment and restricting his wife's rights. Her father disputes the suicide, alleging abuse.

item.title: Shooting at Israeli military site in West Bank leaves two dead, six injured
item.description: A shooting incident at an Israeli Home Front Command military site near Hebron in the West Bank resulted in at least two deaths and six injuries. The Israeli military reported that two assailants were killed after the shooting. An investigation and search operation is ongoing. The incident occurred near the settlement of Telem.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Snow Leopard Population Grows to Approximately 190 Individuals
item.description: On International Snow Leopard Day, Kazakhstan announced a significant recovery in its snow leopard population. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev stated that numbers have risen from a critical low in the 1990s to around 190 individuals. Conservation efforts, including the use of camera traps and satellite collars, are contributing to this resurgence.

item.title: Tajikistan Warns Migrants of Stricter Deportation Rules in Russia
item.description: Tajikistan's labor ministry representation in Russia has alerted citizens about an expanded list of administrative offenses leading to deportation. Effective November 2026, the number of articles in Russia's Code of Administrative Offenses allowing foreigner expulsion will increase from 22 to 45. Fines for certain violations will also be raised.

item.title: TV Project Announced to Combat Distortion of Kazakhstan's History
item.description: A television project has been announced to combat the distortion of Kazakhstan's history. The initiative aims to preserve historical accuracy and national narrative.

item.title: Psychological Services in Education System to Be Strengthened, Research Institute Established
item.description: Uzbekistan's President signed a decree to enhance psychological services in the continuous education system. A Psychology Research Institute is being established on the basis of Tashkent State Pedagogical University.

item.title: Khatlon Region Governor Urges Investors to Fund Cotton Processing
item.description: Davlatali Said, the governor of Khatlon region, has called on domestic and foreign entrepreneurs and investors to invest in cotton processing within the region. The initiative aims to boost local industry.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Foreign Ministry Supports UAE Candidate for UN Secretary-General
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced its support for the candidacy of Lana Zaki Nusseibeh, the UAE's Minister of Foreign Affairs, for the position of UN Secretary-General. The ministry views expanding the pool of candidates as an opportunity for constructive dialogue and finding a mutually acceptable solution amid challenges in the Security Council.

item.title: Over $850,000 Recovered for Uzbek Citizens from Foreign Employers
item.description: During the first nine months of 2026, 817 Uzbek citizens faced issues receiving wages and compensation from foreign employers. The Migration Agency successfully recovered over $850,000 in their favor. The majority of these cases occurred in the Russian Federation.

item.title: Kazakhstan Foreign Minister to Attend Central Asia and Georgia Foreign Ministers' Meeting in Batumi
item.description: Kazakhstan's Foreign Minister Mukhtar Tileuberdi will participate in a meeting of the heads of foreign affairs agencies of Central Asian countries in Batumi on October 23. The meeting will be hosted by Georgia's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister. Ministers from Turkmenistan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan will also attend.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Considers Law Requiring Spouses to Provide Housing After Divorce
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering a legal amendment that would allow courts to compel one spouse to provide temporary housing or pay rent for the other after divorce. The initiative, supported by 11 MPs including the speaker, aims to address the lack of housing guarantees for women post-divorce, citing rising divorce rates and property often registered under husbands' names.

item.title: Illegal Ore Mining Causes Significant Environmental Damage in Karaganda Region
item.description: Illegal ore mining activities in the Karaganda region have resulted in substantial environmental damage. The extent of the ecological harm caused by these illicit operations is significant, highlighting a serious environmental concern.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Competition Committee Investigates Forced Sale of Unneeded Medicines
item.description: Uzbekistan's Committee for the Development of Competition is investigating complaints against pharmaceutical distributors. Reports indicate some importers are forcing the purchase of less demanded drugs along with popular ones, potentially harming smaller businesses and competition.

item.title: World Summit on Child Wellbeing Opens in Samarkand, Uzbekistan
item.description: The World Summit on Investment in Child Wellbeing commenced in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, on October 21, 2026, gathering over 600 participants from more than 100 countries. Organized by the Uzbek government and UN agencies, the forum addresses child protection, education, and healthcare access. UN Secretary-General António Guterres emphasized investing in children's future.

item.title: Illegal Ore Miners Cause Half a Billion Tenge Damage in Kazakhstan's Karaganda Region
item.description: Financial monitoring agents in Kazakhstan's Karaganda region have stopped illegal iron and manganese ore mining near Balkhash city. The operation, conducted without proper permits, caused significant environmental damage. Experts estimate 485 million tenge is needed for land reclamation. Two excavators, a loader, a crushing plant, and dump trucks were used. Three quarries were discovered, with 338,000 cubic meters of soil extracted.

item.title: Tajikistan and Georgia Foreign Ministers Discuss Cooperation in Batumi
item.description: The Foreign Ministers of Tajikistan and Georgia met in Batumi on October 22, 2026, on the sidelines of a regional meeting. They discussed bilateral relations, focusing on trade, economy, transport, communication, and cultural cooperation. Both sides also exchanged views on international agenda issues. The meeting was reported by Tajikistan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

item.title: Unique Ethyleneamine Production Facility to Be Built in Kazakhstan's Aktobe Region
item.description: A new ethyleneamine production facility, representing a significant investment exceeding 100 billion tenge, is planned for the industrial zone in Aktobe, Kazakhstan. The project aims to establish a new direction in mid-tonnage chemistry within the Eurasian Economic Union.

item.title: International Arbitration Rejects Kazakhstan's $12 Billion Claim in Kashagan Dispute
item.description: An international arbitration court has rejected Kazakhstan's claim for approximately $12 billion in disputed costs related to the Kashagan oil field, according to Bloomberg. The court ruled Kazakhstan filed too late for certain expenses incurred between 2011 and 2015, but other claims totaling $8 billion may proceed.

item.title: Zabul Shopkeepers Report Reduced Earnings Due to Border Closure and Rising Costs
item.description: Shopkeepers in Zabul province report that women's earnings from traditional clothing production have decreased due to the closure of trade routes with Pakistan. Increased material costs and weakened sales are impacting both producers and sellers, with some prices falling sharply.

item.title: Global Oil Prices Surge to Five-Month High Amid Middle East Conflict Fears
item.description: Global oil prices have reached a five-month high, with Brent crude trading at $113.17 per barrel. Fears of escalating conflict in the Middle East and potential supply disruptions are driving the increase. Attacks by Houthis on Saudi Arabia and reduced Libyan production have further heightened market concerns about global oil supply.

item.title: Kazakhstan: 485 Million Tenge Needed to Restore Lands After Illegal Mining
item.description: Kazakhstan's Financial Monitoring Agency has stopped illegal iron and manganese ore mining near Balkhash in the Karaganda region. Three illegal quarries were discovered. The agency estimates that 485 million tenge will be required to restore the affected lands and reclaim the quarries. Legal action is ongoing.

item.title: Taliban Leader Urges Fighters to Avoid Tribalism and Nepotism
item.description: Taliban leader Mullah Hebatullah Akhundzada has reportedly instructed his fighters to refrain from 'tribalism and nepotism.' This call comes despite the Taliban government being described as highly ethnically exclusive, primarily favoring Pashtuns. The leader's definition of 'tribalism' appears to focus on prioritizing one's own ethnic group, excluding others, a concept seemingly at odds with his government's composition.
